title: GitHub Copilot in VS Code — August 2026 releases roundup
description: Monthly roundup of Copilot updates shipped for VS Code in August 2026, consolidating the month's incremental releases into one digest.

title: Codex CLI 0.151.0: MCP tool interception, plugin catalogs, sandbox hardening
description: Adds a configurable grace period for discovering tools from optional MCP servers, lets extensions inspect or replace MCP tool results before they reach the model, and combines per-repo plugin catalogs with validation of project marketplaces. Fixes preserve permission profiles across TUI turns, stop /cd from weakening sandbox restrictions, and prevent stale Guardian classifications from authorizing actions after permission changes.

community_feedback.quote: Windows CLI updater offers 0.151.0 but npm latest resolves to 0.149.0.
Intermittent ~55-second tail latency in codex exec on 0.150.1 and 0.151.0.

title: Upcoming changes to GitHub Copilot policies and billing
description: From Sept 1, 2026, new Copilot Business/Enterprise signups reopen for credit card/PayPal customers with upfront per-seat charges (existing card/PayPay customers move to upfront billing Oct 1). No earlier than Sept 28, Copilot Chat on github.com, Chat in Mobile, and the cloud agent merge into one unified experience with chat data retained for the life of the account, and default code review effort shifts from Lite to Balanced.

title: Claude Code v2.1.251: model-switch hooks, agent fleet CLI commands, security fixes
description: Large release (~70 entries): new PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch hooks, live streaming of foreground subagent tool calls to Remote Control, spend-limit bar in /usage, per-session prompt-cache stats in /cost, and new attach/logs/stop/respawn/rm CLI subcommands for managing agent sessions. Also fixes several security issues (symlink permission bypasses, plugin path traversal) and makes Opus 5 the Enterprise seat-based default.

community_feedback.quote: I'm quite surprised that we are not seeing something like this more in the wild. Quite concerning.
Interesting attack, very nicely designed. Not sure if it's much related to the auto mode itself though.
There's plenty of 'optimization' around rubberbanding usage limits as well as routing to a different model in the backend. The incentives are too strong.

title: Copilot code review: resolution reasons, bot PRs and large PRs now supported
description: Copilot code review now reviews PRs authored by bots (including Copilot cloud agent PRs, with full agentic review) and very large PRs — the prior 300-file/20,000-line cap is gone. A new dropdown lets users tag resolved comments as 'Addressed', 'Won't fix', or 'Incorrect' to feed product feedback.

community_feedback.quote: Peer review of changes is still important.
You can't rely on people spotting the significance of such changes.

title: Cursor Cloud Agents can start from scratch without a repo
description: Cloud Agents no longer require a connected GitHub/SCM provider: a 'Start from scratch' option spins up a Cursor Origin repo behind the scenes, and a 'Create repo' button scaffolds agent output into a repo. Live environment preview port-forwards the agent's environment to your browser, with Vercel publishing to a live URL.

title: Claude Code v2.1.248 adds --restricted mode
description: New --restricted launch mode removes code-execution tools and WebFetch, refuses bypassPermissions, and ignores user/project/local settings — for running Claude Code in untrusted or locked-down environments. Also adds per-agent prompt-cache TTL and /usage-credits for AWS Marketplace-billed Enterprise.

title: Codex CLI 0.150.0: @-mention other Codex tasks from the terminal
description: You can now reference other Codex tasks with @ mentions, and agents can read, create, or message tasks from the terminal. Also adds a /copy picker for responses and code blocks, descriptive auto-titles with editable /rename suggestions, clickable Markdown links, permission-mode cycling shortcuts, and ensures untrusted projects can no longer inject project-level AGENTS.md instructions.

title: Gemini CLI v0.57.0: silent retries for capacity errors, multi-turn rollback, TUI hang fix
description: Stable release adding context-aware silent retries and an availability TTL for capacity errors, full rollback of multi-turn requests on cancellation/abort, and execution timeouts that prevent indefinite TUI hangs. Also clarifies privacy notice wording and fixes a misleading admin error for personal accounts.

title: New GitHub Copilot agentic experience in Slack (public preview)
description: Mentioning @GitHub in Slack now starts Copilot agent sessions that answer questions, triage/create issues, investigate failures, implement changes in a secure cloud sandbox, and open PRs. Copilot can also spin up dedicated 'code channels' where teams follow plans, review diffs, and steer the agent collaboratively. Available to Copilot Business/Enterprise orgs in preview.

title: Shared agentic work with GitHub Copilot in Microsoft Teams (public preview)
description: Mentioning @GitHub in a Teams channel, thread, or DM starts a collaborative Copilot agent session everyone can see and steer; teammates with repo write access can have Copilot make code changes that run asynchronously in a secure cloud sandbox. Sessions continue from terminal, Copilot app, or IDE; repo admins can require approval before Copilot-authored PRs merge.

title: Devin Desktop v3.8.20 (formerly Windsurf): Agent Command Center, plan files, multi-root workspaces
description: The editor formerly known as Windsurf (rebranded Devin Desktop in June 2026; windsurf.com/changelog now redirects to the Devin changelog) ships v3.8.20: Agent Command Center follows the selected space and runs multiple agent windows simultaneously, Devin Local gains multi-root workspaces and plan mode that produces a reviewable Markdown plan with an 'Implement' button, individually stoppable subagents, and Devin Cloud adds live streaming shell output and better session filtering.

title: Codex CLI 0.149.0: interactive `codex agents` dashboard and `codex queue`
description: New interactive codex agents dashboard to search, start, open, rename, and stop tasks with configurable shortcuts; codex queue lets you message existing local or remote sessions. Adds /cd, /pwd, and /cwd working-directory commands, expanded Vim editing motions, and codex doctor diagnostics for endpoint-protection and network/proxy failures.

community_feedback.quote: Changes created by Codex had fewer comments in Ruby/Ruby on Rails code. I liked that a lot — Claude is creating verbose comments with recent models and people are tired of it.
'don't write a goddamn novel' — I've said this to Claude way too many times, nothing you can do actually seems to make it significantly less verbose.

title: Gemini CLI v0.56.0 released
description: Routine stable minor release (no highlighted notes in the GitHub release body); follows v0.55.1 with ongoing fixes to IDE connections and eval tooling.

title: Cursor: Cloud Agent Subscriptions, custom modes, isolated subagents, /goal
description: Agents can now subscribe to PRs, Slack threads, or scheduled tasks and wake when events occur (auto-subscribed to their own PRs to fix CI and answer comments). Custom modes pin any skill as always-on, subagents run on isolated VMs with their own environment copy, a new /goal command sets long-lived objectives, and steering messages wait for the next tool call instead of interrupting mid-action.

community_feedback.quote: Goal command on cli - no status - not controls.
Autonomous agents that 'just handle it' create more work, not less.

title: Cursor launches Origin code hosting (early beta)
description: Cursor introduces its own code-hosting service, Origin, in early beta on all paid plans: Origin Repos with a Codebase tab and CLI clone/push, real-time GitHub sync/mirroring, two-way PR comment and review sync with GitHub, agents available in every repo, and app extensions for Vercel, Depot, and Buildkite.

community_feedback.quote: Are there any plans for compatibility with GitHub's APIs? I have a lot of dev tooling which assumes code is stored on public GitHub... This produces some degree of lock-in.
Let's see how strong GitHub's network effect really is... it is worth testing to see how much GitHub's users can tolerate the endless outages and unreliability.
Why not evaluate them on the merits? Is the name really the thing that's important here?
Origin CLI does not run on NixOS or musl linux distros unaltered.
